questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have traveled to Italy with my family loads of times and have always loved the Italian culture. I have also always wanted to try and live abroad for a period or to travel for a long period. When I got the chance to go on exchange, a stay in Bologna was the perfect choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received good information on the check in process of the university in terms of the practical stuff, but not so much in terms of the teaching stuff.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance with checking in online and with signing up for courses at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not very easy, but it was alright. Two friends and I used a webside called
Spacest.com
by Roomless, which worked well - but was pretty expensive due to loads of service fees.
The website also didn't have the best reviews, so we aren't sure if we were just lucky with not getting scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is easier to search for apartments together with someone else, rather than having to find something on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It seems like the registration was opened for exchange students later than for regular students (or maybe we just got the information later), so many courses were filled up once we got to register - which was unfortunate. But we could luckily get help with getting spaces in the filled up courses either way.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You were enrolled in courses through registering them in your OLA. The university then reviewed your OLA and signed you up for the courses, if they were available. 

We had issues with a lot of our wanted courses being filled up, but luckily we were able to get enrolled either ways. We also changed a course a week in to the semester, which wasn't a problem.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online office hours and assistance through e-mail was available. This help was needed, as we initially had loads of problems with being able to attend the needed classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start applying for your courses through your OLA in very good time. In case some of your desired courses are deemed filled up, contact the responsible contact person and plead/argue for attending the course anyway - this worked for us at least.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of my courses was really, really interesting and well executed. But the last three courses were quite poorly executed and just seemed confusing.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were below the level of courses at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The style of teaching was quite similar. I only had lectures and no exercise classes, which is in contrast to at KU. 

Most of the lectures were with digital slides, like at KU. 

The exams were different, as they were all held with pen and paper and nothing else.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Corporate Finance
Economics of Financial Intermediation
Industrial Organization
Public Finance and Public Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would specifically recommend Economics of Financial Intermediation. The lecturer was one of the best I've ever had, as she was very engaging and obviously very, very interested in her field. The course was also a great introduction to financial markets and financial products.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I do not think I encountered any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to restaurants was less expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not make use of any of them, so I cannot really say.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN Bologna hosted lots of different events and trips, but I only participated in a few of them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would probably recommend going to more of the ESN events and trips to meet more exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would REALLY recommend going on trips to different parts of Italy via train. I went to Lerici, Rome, Parma, Modena and Milan - and thoroughly enjoyed all of the trips!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. People were very friendly and welcoming - and a lot of people wanted to speak Italian with you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I unfortunately did not succeed in socializing that much with local students, but I would definitely recommend doing so if possible.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At first I found it challenging with the much slower pace of things compared to Denmark, but gradually you get used to it - and begin enjoying it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The love for food and for enjoying life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Eat lots of good food, go to Bologna FC soccer games and visit San Luca

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start applying for courses in good time. Be aware that the exam sessions are carried out very casually compared to at KU, so try not to get stressed out if the teacher shouws up too late and the whole exam is delayed.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Challenging myself to live away from my friends and family for 5 months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with feeling homesick.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
